title: Plural partitive of common -e words
summary: For these -e words, use the strong consonants and add -ita/-itä: perhe (“family”) → perheitä.
objectives: Form the plural partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

In this selected e-word family, add -ita/-itä after e, using the word’s strong consonant form. For tuote and osoite, strengthen t to tt first. This can also be understood as the strong plural stem ending in -ei- plus -ta/-tä. These plural forms differ from the singular -etta/-että pattern.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Keep perhe and add -itä: perhe → perheitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “family”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep huone and add -ita: huone → huoneita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “room”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep kirje and add -itä: kirje → kirjeitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “letter”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep vene and add -itä: vene → veneitä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “boat”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep kone and add -ita: kone → koneita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “machine”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep hame and add -ita: hame → hameita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “skirt”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

examples.english: product · t → tt, then add -ita after e
steps: Strengthen t to tt, then add -ita after e: tuote → tuotteita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “product”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

examples.english: address · t → tt, then add -ita after e
steps: Strengthen t to tt, then add -ita after e: osoite → osoitteita.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “address”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Do not use the singular -tta/-ttä ending for this plural.
Do not double e before adding -ita/-itä.
Strengthen t in tuotteita and osoitteita.
